# Constant-denominator approximation in the HCR neuron: numerical check
*(all numbers generated by code from results/results.csv; seed 12345, n=2e+06 samples per (type, rho_S))*

**Setup.** One HCR neuron, d=3 (output x, inputs y,z), Gaussian-copula ground truth, Legendre basis of degree m∈{2,4,6}, coefficients by direct moment estimation. Inputs' dependence is set by Spearman rho_S∈[0,0.9]; neuron types SUM (r_xy=r_xz=0.5) and CONTRAST (r_xy=+c, r_xz=−c). Incoming belief q: S1 (q=D), S2 flat, S3a–d Beta products (S3c = conflicting, S3d = narrow). Compared: DUDA (the paper's constant-denominator formula, Eq. 10), EXACT_UNCAL (E_q[N/D], defined only if D≥0.01 on supp q), EXACT_CAL (max(N,eps) + per-(y,z) normalisation) and GOLD (analytic copula conditional). Errors are total-variation (TV) distances; d_denom=TV(DUDA,EXACT_UNCAL), d_neg=TV(EXACT_UNCAL,EXACT_CAL), d_model=TV(·,GOLD), d_total=TV(DUDA,GOLD).
Tests: T1 PASS, T2 PASS, T3 PASS, T4 PASS, T5 PASS, T6 PASS, T7 PASS, T8 PASS, T9 FAIL (documented) (see Deviations), T10 PASS (reduced re-run).

## Thresholds (m = 4; rho_S where the error first reaches the level; — = not reached before D<0 makes the exact ratio undefined, or up to 0.9)
| type | m | belief | d_denom≥1% | d_denom≥5% | var.err≥5% | var.err≥20% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CONTRAST | 4 | S1 | 0.07 | 0.37 | 0.16 | — |
| CONTRAST | 4 | S2 | 0.06 | 0.23 | 0.14 | — |
| CONTRAST | 4 | S3a | 0.26 | — | 0.39 | — |
| CONTRAST | 4 | S3b | 0.26 | — | 0.38 | — |
| CONTRAST | 4 | S3c | 0.09 | 0.31 | 0.38 | — |
| CONTRAST | 4 | S3d | — | — | — | — |
| SUM | 4 | S1 | 0.07 | 0.39 | 0.18 | — |
| SUM | 4 | S2 | 0.09 | — | 0.25 | — |
| SUM | 4 | S3a | — | — | — | — |
| SUM | 4 | S3b | 0.16 | — | — | — |
| SUM | 4 | S3c | — | — | — | — |
| SUM | 4 | S3d | — | — | — | — |

For m=4, D becomes negative at rho_S≈0.44 (SUM) and 0.43 (CONTRAST); the exact ratio is undefined from rho_S=0.50 / 0.50 on a 0.1 grid. All m and the min D<D_floor onset: results/thresholds.csv.

## Answers
**Q1 – when does the constant-denominator error become noticeable?** With a flat belief (S2, m=4), d_denom is 2.0% (SUM) and 4.1% (CONTRAST) at rho_S=0.2, and reaches 1% already at rho_S≈0.09 / 0.06. For the neuron's own density (S1) the signed relative variance error is 5.5% (SUM) and -6.4% (CONTRAST) at rho_S=0.2. For a narrow belief (S3d) it is small: d_denom=0.0005 (SUM) and 0.0039 (CONTRAST) at rho_S=0.3. The effect therefore depends strongly on how wide the incoming belief is (rho_S=0.3, m=4, d_denom, SUM / CONTRAST: S1 0.039/0.043, S2 0.026/0.069, S3b 0.015/0.012, S3c 0.004/0.048, S3a 0.002/0.012, S3d 0.001/0.004).

**Q2 – d_denom vs d_neg vs d_model.** At rho_S=0.2 (m=4, eps=0.01): SUM/S2: d_denom 0.020, d_neg 0.001, d_model_uncal 0.004 -> largest: d_denom; SUM/S3c: d_denom 0.002, d_neg 0.001, d_model_uncal 0.009 -> largest: d_model_uncal; CONTRAST/S2: d_denom 0.041, d_neg 0.010, d_model_uncal 0.011 -> largest: d_denom; CONTRAST/S3c: d_denom 0.027, d_neg 0.014, d_model_uncal 0.013 -> largest: d_denom. Where D<0 (rho_S=0.5, 0.8) the exact ratio is undefined and only d_model_cal, d_dc and d_total remain:

| type/belief | rho_S | d_model_cal | d_dc | d_total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUM/S2 | 0.5 | 0.010 | 0.024 | 0.029 |
| SUM/S3c | 0.5 | 0.011 | 0.003 | 0.008 |
| CONTRAST/S2 | 0.5 | 0.043 | 0.102 | 0.125 |
| CONTRAST/S3c | 0.5 | 0.031 | 0.082 | 0.101 |
| SUM/S2 | 0.8 | 0.063 | 0.031 | 0.032 |
| SUM/S3c | 0.8 | 0.050 | 0.052 | 0.008 |
| CONTRAST/S2 | 0.8 | 0.217 | 0.107 | 0.298* |
| CONTRAST/S3c | 0.8 | 0.223 | 0.122 | 0.291* |
(* GOLD quadrature-limited)

The labels show which component dominates per case at rho_S=0.2. For CONTRAST/S2, d_total reaches 0.30 at rho_S=0.8 (GOLD variance 0.139 vs DUDA 0.083; GOLD there is quadrature-limited, see Deviations).

**Q3 – variance vs mean.** In 89% of the 149 defined (rho_S>0) configurations the relative variance error exceeds the absolute mean error. Median ratio |rel. var. err|/|Δmean| at m=4: S1 4649, S2 604, S3c 14; maximum errors (m=4): S1 variance 11.4% vs mean 0.0001; S2 19.0% vs 0.0003; S3c 5.8% vs 0.0375. The mean is nearly preserved, the variance is not; with conflicting beliefs (S3c) the mean error is no longer negligible.

**Q4 – sensitivity.** *eps:* for SUM/S3c/m=4, d_model_cal at rho_S=0.7/0.8/0.9 is 0.023/0.049/0.075 (eps=0.1), 0.019/0.050/0.143 (0.01), 0.018/0.049/0.168 (0.001), while d_total of DUDA is 0.008/0.008/0.008: naive clipping can be farther from GOLD than the ratio of expectations here. *m:* at rho_S=0.3, S2, d_denom for m=2/4/6 is 0.027/0.026/0.024 (SUM) and 0.065/0.069/0.063 (CONTRAST): weak m-dependence, but the onset of D<0 moves earlier with m. *Stabiliser?* Over the 145 valid rows where EXACT_UNCAL is undefined (eps=0.01), DUDA is closer to GOLD than EXACT_CAL in 32% (excluding GOLD-quadrature-limited rows: 39% of 121); eps=0.1: 29%, eps=0.001: 33%. DUDA stays defined and finite there, but it is not systematically more accurate than a calibrated conditional – it depends on belief and rho_S: SUM/S3c at rho_S=0.8: d_total 0.008 vs d_model_cal 0.050 (DUDA closer); CONTRAST/S2 at rho_S=0.5: 0.125 vs 0.043 (calibrated conditional closer).

## Optional stages (exploratory)
*Taylor-corrected denominator (m=4, SUM/S2, TV to EXACT_UNCAL, K=0/1/2):* rho_S=0.1: 0.0116/0.0022/0.0009; 0.2: 0.0196/0.0092/0.0078; 0.3: 0.0258/0.0224/0.0291; 0.4: 0.0353/0.0412/0.0758. It helps at small rho_S (K=2 best at 0.1–0.2), is marginal at 0.3 (K=1 0.0224 vs 0.0258, K=2 worse) and is worse from 0.4 (the series condition |1−D|<1 on supp q fails for SUM/S2 from rho_S=0.2 on, max|1−D| on supp q is 1.42 at rho_S=0.2; last rho_S where the condition holds: 0.10). CONTRAST/S3c, rho_S=0.1/0.2/0.4: K=0 0.0107/0.0274/0.0789, K=2 0.0003/0.0024/0.0241.
*Does a value (MSE) loss reduce negativity / propagation error?* (a_1jk, a_0jk trained, L-BFGS ≤500 its, 2e5 samples; before→after):

| type | rho_S | test MSE | min D | area D<0 | status (nit) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUM | 0.2 | 0.0503→0.0502 | 0.39→-0.04 | 0.0%→0.0% | 0 (40) |
| SUM | 0.5 | 0.902→0.0669 | -0.12→-0.11 | 1.3%→1.0% | 1 (500) |
| SUM | 0.8 | 13.4→0.0719 | -0.71→-0.98 | 8.6%→8.5% | 1 (500) |
| CONTRAST | 0.2 | 0.0328→0.0323 | 0.36→-0.00 | 0.0%→0.0% | 0 (207) |
| CONTRAST | 0.5 | 1.18→0.0422 | -0.13→-0.15 | 1.3%→1.3% | 1 (500) |
| CONTRAST | 0.8 | 1.18e+03→2.31 | -0.70→-0.93 | 8.6%→8.8% | 1 (500) |

Largest change of d_total (S2,S3c) after training: improvement 0.0020, deterioration 0.0056. The test MSE drops sharply where the direct estimates have B≤0 on some samples (rho_S≥0.5), but the area with D<0 changes by at most 0.26 percentage points (rho_S≥0.5) and min D is not systematically raised; runs at rho_S≥0.5 stopped at the iteration limit (status 1, not converged). One optimiser, one run, only a_0jk and a_1jk trained – no conclusion.

## Limitations
Single neuron, d=3, Gaussian copula, low degrees (m≤6), no deep network and no end-to-end training; S2 (flat belief) is not the data distribution of (y,z), so DUDA(S2)=Σa_i00 f_i is the model's x-marginal while GOLD(S2) is not uniform even for a perfect model – part of d_total in S2 is this prior mismatch, not an HCR defect. EXACT_CAL uses per-(y,z) conditional normalisation (a harsher calibration than the paper's neglect of it); the paper's own remedy is correction by training, which is only probed in Stage 9. Sampling noise (n=2e6) enters through a_ijk (median SE of a_011 ≈ 6.8e-04).

## Deviations / quadrature
24 of 360 rows (all CONTRAST: S2, S3a, S3b, S3c; rho_S≥0.6) are flagged `quadrature_limited`: the (y,z) integral is converged (401 vs 801 normal-score nodes identical) but GOLD(x) develops integrable spikes at x→0,1 that a fixed x-grid cannot resolve; ∫GOLD=0.9980 at rho_S=0.6 and 0.891 at 0.9 on 192 x-nodes; TV(DUDA,GOLD) changes from 0.391 (192) to 0.413 (1000 x-nodes) at rho_S=0.9, and 0.1690→0.1698 at 0.6. T9: STRICT criterion (all rows, rho_S<=0.6): max |TV change| 192->256 = 2.58e-04 in d_model_cal (<1e-4 required); excluding rows flagged quadrature_limited (GOLD x-grid singular edges, 9 such rows at rho_S<=0.6): 9.83e-05; rho_S>=0.7 observed (reported): 4.95e-03 all rows, 2.26e-04 excluding flagged; defined-flag changes: 0.. T10 was verified on a reduced re-run only.

## Three talking points (measurements, not criticism)
1. With a flat belief, m=4 and rho_S=0.2, replacing E[N/D] by E[N]/E[D] changes the output density by 2.0% (SUM) / 4.1% (CONTRAST) in TV; for a narrow belief at rho_S=0.3 it is 0.0005 / 0.0039.
2. The mean survives (|Δmean|≤0.0003 for S1/S2) while the variance error reaches 19.0%; this is where the approximation is visible.
3. Dr Duda's point about negative densities is measurable: D<0 starts at rho_S≈0.44 (m=4), after which the exact ratio is undefined and only calibrated or ratio-of-expectation forms exist; whether training removes this was probed only once (Stage 9) with no systematic reduction of the negative area.
